sn35.132:1.1: On one occasion the Venerable Mahakaccana was dwelling among the people of Avanti in a forest hut at Makkarakaṭa.
sn35.132:1.2: Then a number of brahmin youths, students of the brahmin Lohicca, while collecting firewood, approached the Venerable Mahakaccana’s forest hut. Having approached, they stomped and trampled all around the hut, and in a boisterous and noisy manner they played various pranks, saying:
sn35.132:1.3: “These shaveling ascetics, menials, swarthy offspring of the Lord’s feet, are honoured, respected, esteemed, worshipped, and venerated by their servile devotees.”
sn35.132:1.4: Then the Venerable Mahakaccana came out of his dwelling and said to those brahmin youths:
sn35.132:1.6: I will speak to you on the Dhamma.”
sn35.132:1.7: When this was said, those youths became silent.
sn35.132:1.8: Then the Venerable Mahakaccana addressed those youths with verses:
sn35.132:2.1: “Those men of old who excelled in virtue,
sn35.132:2.2: Those brahmins who recalled the ancient rules,
sn35.132:2.3: Their sense doors guarded, well protected,
sn35.132:3.1: They took delight in Dhamma and meditation,
sn35.132:3.2: Those brahmins who recalled the ancient rules.
sn35.132:4.2: Puffed up by clan, faring unrighteously,
sn35.132:4.3: Overcome by anger, armed with diverse weapons,
sn35.132:4.4: They molest both frail and firm.
sn35.132:5.1:
“For one with sense doors unguarded
All the vows he undertakes are vain
sn35.132:5.2: Just like the wealth a man gains in a dream:
sn35.132:5.3: Fasting and sleeping on the ground,
sn35.132:5.4: Bathing at dawn, study of the three Vedas,
sn35.132:6.1: Rough hides, matted locks, and dirt;
sn35.132:6.6: Are used to increase their worldly gains.
sn35.132:7.4: That is the path for attaining Brahma.”
sn35.132:8.1: Then those brahmin youths, angry and displeased, approached the brahmin Lohicca and told him:
sn35.132:8.2: “See now, sir, you should know that the ascetic Mahakaccana categorically denigrates and scorns the hymns of the brahmins.”
sn35.132:8.3: When this was said, the brahmin Lohicca was angry and displeased.
sn35.132:8.4: But then it occurred to him:
sn35.132:8.5: “It is not proper for me to abuse and revile the ascetic Mahakaccana solely on the basis of what I have heard from these youths.
sn35.132:8.6: Let me approach him and inquire.”
sn35.132:9.1: Then the brahmin Lohicca, together with those brahmin youths, approached the Venerable Mahakaccana. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Mahakaccana and,
sn35.132:9.2: when they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn35.132:9.3: “Master Kaccana, did a number of brahmin youths, my students, come this way while collecting firewood?”
sn35.132:9.5: “Did Master Kaccana have any conversation with them?”
sn35.132:9.6: “I did have a conversation with them, brahmin.”
sn35.132:9.7: “What kind of conversation did you have with them, Master Kaccana?”
sn35.132:9.8: “The conversation I had with those youths was like this:
sn35.132:10.1: “‘Those men of old who excelled in virtue,
sn35.132:10.2: Those brahmins who recalled the ancient rules,
sn35.132:10.5: That is the path for attaining Brahma.’
sn35.132:11.1: Such was the conversation that I had with those youths.”
sn35.132:12.2: In what way, Master Kaccana, is one ‘with sense doors unguarded’?”
sn35.132:12.3: “Here, brahmin, having seen a form with the eye, someone is intent upon a pleasing form and repelled by a displeasing form. He dwells without having set up mindfulness of the body, with a limited mind,
sn35.132:12.4: and he does not understand as it really is that liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, wherein those evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.
sn35.132:12.5: Having heard a sound with the ear …
sn35.132:12.9: Having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, someone is intent upon a pleasing mental phenomenon and repelled by a displeasing mental phenomenon. He dwells without having set up mindfulness of the body …
sn35.132:12.11: It is in such a way, brahmin, that one is ‘with sense doors unguarded.’”
sn35.132:12.12: “It is wonderful, Master Kaccana! It is amazing, Master Kaccana!
sn35.132:12.13: How Master Kaccana has declared one whose sense doors are actually unguarded to be one ‘with sense doors unguarded’!
sn35.132:13.1: But Master Kaccana said ‘with sense doors guarded.’
sn35.132:13.2: In what way, Master Kaccana, is one ‘with sense doors guarded’?”
sn35.132:13.3: “Here, brahmin, having seen a form with the eye, someone is not intent upon a pleasing form and not repelled by a displeasing form. He dwells having set up mindfulness of the body, with a measureless mind,
sn35.132:13.4: and he understands as it really is that liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, wherein those evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.
sn35.132:13.5: Having heard a sound with the ear …
sn35.132:13.9: Having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, someone is not intent upon a pleasing mental phenomenon and not repelled by a displeasing mental phenomenon. He dwells having set up mindfulness of the body …
sn35.132:13.11: It is in such a way, brahmin, that one is ‘with sense doors guarded.’”
sn35.132:14.1: “It is wonderful, Master Kaccana! It is amazing, Master Kaccana!
sn35.132:14.2: How Master Kaccana has declared one whose sense doors are actually guarded to be one ‘with sense doors guarded’!
sn35.132:14.3: Magnificent, Master Kaccana! Magnificent, Master Kaccana!
sn35.132:14.4: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Kaccana … as in §127 …
sn35.132:14.6: From today let Master Kaccana remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.
sn35.132:14.7: “Let Master Kaccana approach the Lohicca family just as he approaches the families of the lay followers in Makkarakaṭa.
sn35.132:14.8: The brahmin youths and maidens there will pay homage to Master Kaccana, they will stand up for him out of respect, they will offer him a seat and water, and that will lead to their welfare and happiness for a long time.”
